subject: Prefetch resync window and proposed credit path
messages:
From: Sophie Park <sophie.park@fastlane.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@fastlane.com
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: spike in 503/429s during prefetch window (0900-0930 PDT)

Hannah —

We observed a sustained elevation in 503s and 429 bursts starting ~09:02 PDT and lasting until ~09:26 PDT for our checkout path. Our dashboards show a mismatch between the token-prefetch layer and the KV cache (many prefetched keys returning misses, causing backpressure). This resulted in increased tail latency and several checkout failures during our morning peak.

We've attached a small telemetry snapshot and would like confirmation on whether this qualifies for SLA remediation (proportional credit). We saw a 3.4% availability delta against the 99.95% monthly target during the window. Can you confirm next steps and what evidence you need from us?

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement — this is customer-impacting for us.

Thanks,
Sophie
Ops Lead, FastLane Payments

Attachments: fastlane_telemetry_snapshot_2028-10-02.zip (telemetry ZIP, 6MB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@fastlane.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: spike in 503/429s during prefetch window (0900-0930 PDT)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the snapshot. I’ve looped in David (infra) and Laura (account & entitlement) to triage. Preliminary ack: we saw a correlated prefetched-key miss spike in our telemetry and an autoscaler reaction that increased tail latency in the same window.

Actions we’ll take immediately:
- David: will pull the full prefetched-key hit/miss traces and the orchestrator logs for 08:45–09:40 PDT.
- Laura: will start an entitlement check to estimate proportional remediation if the window meets SLA criteria.
- Hannah: I’ll confirm the exact incident window and share an evidence packet back to you within 24 hours.

Can you confirm whether FastLane has any client-side batching changes or new routing rules that started at 09:00 PDT? That will help attribution.

— Hannah
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sophie Park <sophie.park@fastlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: spike in 503/429s during prefetch window (0900-0930 PDT)

Sophie / Hannah —

I pulled the orchestrator and prefetch traces. Quick summary: between 09:01:48 and 09:25:52 PDT we saw a cluster of prefetched-key miss rates jump from ~0.7% baseline to 18.6%, which caused elevated KV cache fetches and a temporary queue saturation on the inference frontends handling the checkout route. There were short-lived 503s (~1–2m each) propagated back to the client and transient 429 rate increases as our backpressure kicked in.

Items for FastLane to validate on your side:
- Any sudden increase in tokenization requests or changed input size distribution at 09:00–09:05?
- Client-side retries that may have amplified load?

Attached: an excerpt from the prefetch logs and a draft prorate calculation for proportional credit based on impacted tokens and request surface.

Next steps from our side:
- We’re packaging the full evidence bundle (telemetry, ingress traces, autoscaler snapshots) and will upload to the shared Drive link.
- If FastLane confirms no client-side change, Laura will propose a remediation credit and I’ll kick off a postmortem cadence.

Thanks,
David
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_prefetch_log_excerpt.txt; proposed_prorate_calculation.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@fastlane.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: spike in 503/429s during prefetch window (0900-0930 PDT)

Sophie —

Thanks for the quick collaboration. We reviewed David’s evidence and the telemetry you provided. At this stage our proposed path is: 

1) Evidence bundle: we will deliver the complete package (logs, ingress traces, scaler snapshots, and the prefetch delta calculation) to the Drive link by EOD today.
2) Entitlement assessment: based on the 09:01:48–09:25:52 PDT window and the 3.4% availability delta you reported, the incident appears within scope for proportional remedy under the SLA. We will calculate a prorated credit using the draft workbook and share the proposed credit amount by Friday COB.
3) Postmortem: we propose a joint postmortem meeting (30 minutes) the week after next to align on root cause, fixes, and mitigations (prefetch resync safeguards and KV cache warming). Please indicate preferred windows (I’ve tentatively proposed Tue 10/16 10:00–10:30 PDT on the Drive calendar).
4) Temporary mitigations we’ll apply: near-term prefetch resync during low-traffic hours and a rule to limit concurrent prefetch concurrency for the checkout route while we finish the root cause fix.

If FastLane confirms no client-side changes at 09:00–09:05, we’ll proceed with the credit calculation and schedule the postmortem. If there are client changes, we’ll document attribution in the postmortem but still share the evidence bundle.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Account Services — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
